title: Hiring Panel resume (the source of truth for .docx, .pdf and .md)
description: One JSON drives every output format. Evidence, ops, meta.addressed and meta.cuts are never rendered; they exist so every line can be traced back to the candidate's own words (R# resume lines in work/inputs/ledger.json, Q# answers in work/answers.json). The job posting (J#) is never evidence. hp.rewrite.truth checks the claims; hp.render renders the file.

ref.description: R12 (one resume line), R12-R14 (a range of lines) or Q2 (an answer). Never J# (the posting is never evidence).

src.description: orig = a line of the uploaded resume (R#); user = an answer the candidate gave (Q#).

quote.description: Verbatim snippet of the cited line or answer (case and whitespace insensitive). For keyword answers, quote a yes/some item's term or detail, or other words of the reply; never a term answered 'no'.

date.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or 'present'. Only the precision the source had; otherwise use dateText.

text.description: Final wording. May contain {{placeholderId}} tokens and **bold**. Sentence case. No emoji or symbols.

textIfUnknown.description: The honest version without the missing fact. Required whenever text has a {{placeholder}}.

jdTerms.description: Posting terms this bullet now uses (only where the evidence shows the same thing).

originalText.description: The source wording, for the before/after view.

role.description: The title as the source has it, or an honest label the cited lines show: Family Caregiver, Volunteer, Student, Freelancer, Self-employed, Personal Project.

name.description: Project, certification, award or activity name. Shown in bold, followed by context and org ('BLS Provider | American Heart Association').

context.description: Project context, e.g. 'Marketing Analytics class project'.

dateText.description: Verbatim date when the source was imprecise ('Summer 2025'). Wins over start/end.

locale.description: BCP-47, e.g. en-US. en-US and en-CA render on Letter, everything else on A4 (hp/data/locale_norms.json when present).

targetPages.description: null turns the page target off (academic or federal CVs).

stage.description: Picks the locale's default page target when targetPages is absent.

layout.description: classic = dates right-aligned on a tab stop (a space precedes every tab); inline = dates after ' | '.

role.description: The title as the source has it, or an honest label the cited lines show: Family Caregiver, Volunteer, Student, Freelancer, Self-employed, Personal Project.

labels.description: Renderer words for non-English resumes (write them in the resume's language).

addressed.description: What the rewrite did about each ranked issue (synthesis issue ids). The report's status column reads this.

cuts.description: Every source line dropped from the new resume, with a reason. Never drop real experience silently.

headline.description: Optional one-liner built only from evidenced facts.

location.description: City, region. Never a full street address.

sections.description: Rendered in this order (REORDER happens here).

title.description: A standard heading in the resume's language: Education, Experience, Projects, Leadership & Activities, Volunteer Experience, Skills, Certifications, Awards, Summary. Any other word must come from the lines the section cites (the truth check raises HEADING_CLAIM for 'Clinical Experience' over non-clinical work); honest labels such as 'Family Caregiving' pass when a cited answer shows them.

placeholders.description: Missing facts the panel wants, keyed by the id used as {{id}} in a bullet or summary.

ask.description: The plain-language question asked in the batch.

label.description: Short hint shown in draft mode: [ADD: label].

value.description: The candidate's answer with their hedging kept ('about 600', '50-100').

question.description: The answers.json id that holds the value.
